candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — use infection-control precautions, maintain aseptic technique, and safely manage invasive devices/access sites
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hemodialysis catheter access / bloodstream-infection prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Use aseptic technique and appropriate catheter-hub disinfection every time a hemodialysis central venous catheter is connected, disconnected, or otherwise accessed.

options.A: Use aseptic catheter-access technique and disinfect the catheter hubs with an appropriate antiseptic before access
options.B: Use clean nonsterile technique because aseptic technique is needed only when the catheter is first inserted
options.C: Skip hub disinfection when the catheter cap appears visibly clean
options.D: Reserve aseptic technique for scheduled dressing changes and use routine handling for dialysis connections

candidate.rationale: CDC dialysis infection-prevention guidance requires adherence to aseptic technique when connecting and disconnecting hemodialysis catheters and during dressing changes. Catheter hubs should be scrubbed with an appropriate antiseptic after the cap is removed and before access, every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected. Maximal sterile barrier precautions are an insertion procedure standard and should not be incorrectly generalized to every routine catheter access. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hemodialysis catheter connection/disconnection and dressing care require aseptic technique, with hub disinfection before each access/disconnection.
candidate.source_document_title: Best Practices for Bloodstream Infection Prevention in Dialysis Setting
